title_en: Guangdong Longzheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. and Guangdong Jingmao Auction House Co., Ltd. — Application for Reconsideration of Enforcement
ruling_gist_en: In cases where the buyer and the shareholders of the auction house are relatives, unless it can be proven that other unrelated bidders participated in the auction and conducted full competitive bidding, collusion between the auction house and the buyer may be found; if the buyer colludes with the auction house and knows that the appraised price and transaction price of the subject matter are too low, then the buyer and the auction house constitute malice with respect to the infringement of rights of the right holders related to the subject matter caused by the auction. The people's court may, in accordance with law, declare the auction void or set it aside.

full_text_en:
Guangdong Longzheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. and Guangdong Jingmao Auction House Co., Ltd. — Application for Review of Enforcement

【Ruling Summary】

In a case where the purchaser and the shareholders of the auction house are all relatives, unless it can be proven that other unrelated bidders participated in the auction and conducted sufficient competitive bidding, it may be determined that there was collusion between the auction house and the purchaser. If the purchaser and the auction house have engaged in collusion and knew that the appraised price and the transaction price of the subject matter were too low, then the purchaser and the auction house have acted maliciously in causing the auction to infringe upon the rights of persons entitled to the subject matter. The People's Court may lawfully declare the auction void or set aside the auction.

Enforcement Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Zhi Fu Zi No. 6

Applicant for Review: Guangdong Longzheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. Address: 18th Floor, Times International Tower, 187 Dongfeng West Road, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xiongwei, General Manager of the Company.

Applicant for Review: Guangdong Jingmao Auction House Co., Ltd. Address: Room 1708, 17th Floor, Times International Tower, 187 Dongfeng West Road, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Aihong, General Manager of the Company.

Applicant for Enforcement: Guangzhou Baiyun Lifa Industrial Company. Address: Room 311, Feixia Building, Zhongshan Eighth Road, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Pan Zhizhao, Manager of the Company.

Party Subject to Enforcement: Guangzhou Guangfeng Real Estate Construction Co., Ltd. Address: 3rd Floor, No. 5, Guangzhou Avenue North, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Jian Zuyang, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Party Subject to Enforcement: Guangzhou Yinfeng Real Estate Co., Ltd. Address: 2nd Floor, No. 5, Guangzhou Avenue North, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Jian Zuyang, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Party Subject to Enforcement: Guangzhou Jinhui Real Estate Construction Co., Ltd. Address: 3rd Floor, No. 5, Guangzhou Avenue North, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Jian Zuyang, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The Applicants for Review, Guangdong Longzheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. and Guangdong Jingmao Auction House Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2011) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Yi Zi No. 1 of the Guangdong High People's Court, hereby apply to this Court for review. This Court formed a collegial panel to conduct examination, and now the examination is concluded.

This Court finds: In the case of illegal lending dispute between Guangzhou Baiyun Lifa Industrial Company (hereinafter referred to as Lifa Company) and Guangzhou Guangfeng Real Estate Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangfeng Company), Guangzhou Yinfeng Real Estate Co., Ltd., and Guangzhou Jinhui Real Estate Construction Co., Ltd., the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Guangdong High Court) rendered a civil judgment (1996) Yue Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 4 on May 20, 1997, ordering Guangfeng Company and Guangzhou Yinfeng Real Estate Co., Ltd. to jointly repay Lifa Company a loan of RMB 160,647,776.07 and interest, and ordering Guangzhou Jinhui Real Estate Construction Co., Ltd. to bear joint and several compensatory liability.

In the course of enforcing the aforesaid judgment, on February 11, 1998, the Guangdong High Court ordered the seizure of the unsold portion of the property of Guangfeng Building under the name of Guangfeng Company (the entire first floor; the entire sixteenth floor; the negative first floor except for the 110-square-meter parking spaces already sold; and a total of 71 units on the fifth, sixth, eighth, ninth, tenth, twelfth, thirteenth, and fourteenth floors, with a total area of 18,851.86 square meters). The next day, it entrusted Guangdong Jingmao Auction House Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingmao Auction House) to conduct the auction. In June of the same year, the Guangdong Yuecai Real Estate Appraisal Office entrusted by the court issued an appraisal report concluding that the auction price of the aforesaid portion of Guangfeng Building as of June 12, 1998 was RMB 102,493,594. Subsequently, the case was suspended from disposal for certain reasons.

In early 2001, the Guangdong High Court resumed the disposal procedure and on April 4 of the same year entrusted Jingmao Auction House to auction the entire Guangfeng Building. In early November 2001, the Guangdong High Court published a notice in newspapers announcing the proposed auction of the entire Guangfeng Building, requiring all persons entitled to rights in Guangfeng Building or purchasers of units to declare their rights and register with Jingmao Auction House before November 30, 2001, pending handling by the Guangdong High Court. In accordance with the notice, the following rights were declared to Jingmao Auction House: claims for delivery of pre-sold units of Guangfeng Building, claims for return of relocated units, and claims for refund of purchase money, project payments, bank loans, etc., amounting to over RMB 1.5 billion, of which the purchase money paid by purchasers exceeded RMB 200 million.

On August 26, 2003, the Guangdong High Court entrusted Guangdong Caixing Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. (formerly Guangdong Yuecai Real Estate Appraisal Office) to appraise the entire Guangfeng Building. On September 10 of the same year, the appraisal office issued an appraisal report concluding that the market value of the entire Guangfeng Building (land area of 3,009 square meters, building area of 34,840 square meters) was RMB 34.45 million, and recommended that the reserve price for auction be 70% of the market value, i.e., RMB 24.12 million. On October 17, 2003, Jingmao Auction House auctioned the entire Guangfeng Building to Guangdong Longzheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longzheng Company) for RMB 24.12 million. On October 28, 2003, the Guangdong High Court issued a civil ruling (1997) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 7, affirming the transfer of the entire Guangfeng Building to Longzheng Company for RMB 24.12 million. On January 5, 2004, the court issued a notice of assistance to the Guangzhou Municipal Land and Housing Authority, requesting the transfer of ownership of the entire Guangfeng Building to the purchaser Longzheng Company, "discharging and canceling all relations and contracts or agreements concerning the sale, transfer, mortgage, demolition compensation, etc., of the Guangfeng Building properties," and declaring that all persons entitled to rights in the original Guangfeng Building, including purchasers, transferees, mortgagees, persons whose property is demolished, or relocated households, shall have their rights handled by the court in accordance with law. After acquiring Guangfeng Building, Longzheng Company continued to invest funds for completion construction on the basis of the original main frame structure, and after completion renamed it "Times International Tower."

In October 2008, the Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate, after investigating the auction of Guangfeng Building based on a report, concluded that Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser Longzheng Company were actually controlled by the same person and had engaged in self-selling and self-buying in the auction of Guangfeng Building, which violated the relevant provisions of the Auction Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Auction Law); that the two appraisal conclusions of Guangdong Yuecai Real Estate Appraisal Office for Guangfeng Building showed a huge discrepancy, and the entrusting court was lax in supervision, resulting in the undervaluation of Guangfeng Building, seriously infringing upon the interests of small property owners who had pre-purchased units, etc., and requested that the Guangdong High Court handle the matter according to law.

On June 2, 2011, the Guangdong High Court issued an Enforcement Ruling (1997) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 7-1, determining that the shareholders of Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser Longzheng Company were all relatives, indicating an affiliated relationship. The discrepancy between the two appraised prices of Guangfeng Building was huge: the first appraisal covered about half of the building's area, and the second appraisal covered the entire building, but the second appraised price was only 35% of the first, and even considering market changes, the change in price was obviously abnormal. According to the report of Jingmao Auction House, three bidders participated in the auction, but the other two bidders did not raise a paddle to bid, and Longzheng Company won the auction with a single bid at the starting price of RMB 24.12 million. However, after the court coordinated with relevant judicial authorities, the two bidders could not be located. Subsequently, the court issued a written notice to Jingmao Auction House requesting the bidding materials of these two bidders, but Jingmao Auction House failed to provide them as required. Jingmao Auction House also did not file with the administrative department for industry and commerce in accordance with Article 4 of the Interim Measures for Supervision and Administration of Auction, which provides that "an auction enterprise holding an auction activity shall file for record with the administrative department for industry and commerce at the location of the auction activity seven days before the auction date,... and the auction enterprise shall, within seven days after the conclusion of the auction, file the list of bidders and copies of their identity certificates with the administrative department for industry and commerce at the location of the auction activity for record." Existing evidence could not confirm that the other two bidders actually participated in the auction. In summary, it could be determined that the auctioneer Jingmao Auction House and the bidder Longzheng Company had engaged in malicious collusion in the auction of Guangfeng Building, resulting in the inability to conduct a fair competitive bidding for the auction of Guangfeng Building, thereby harming the interests of purchasers and other creditors. Pursuant to Article 58 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC and Article 65 of the Auction Law, the court ruled the auction void and set aside the civil ruling (1997) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 7 issued by the court on October 28, 2003. In response, the purchaser Longzheng Company and Jingmao Auction House each raised objections to the Guangdong High Court. Upon review, on October 9, 2011, the Guangdong High Court issued an Enforcement Ruling (2011) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Yi Zi No. 1, upholding the original ruling and rejecting the objections. The two objectors then applied to this Court for review, seeking to set aside the aforesaid objection ruling and the original ruling.

The reasons for review submitted by Longzheng Company and Jingmao Auction House are consolidated and summarized as follows: There is a reasonable explanation for the huge discrepancy between the two appraised values of Guangfeng Building, and both appraisals were conducted by appraisal institutions entrusted by the court, so the appraisal results are irrelevant to the auction house and the purchaser. The reserve price was determined by the Guangdong High Court based on the actual circumstances at the time, and the transaction price was caused by objective market factors at the time, without any human factors. In accordance with the provisions of the Interim Measures for Supervision and Administration of Auction, Jingmao Auction House filed for record with the Tianhe Branch of the Guangzhou Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce on October 9, 2003, before the auction of Guangfeng Building, and on October 22 after the auction, and the branch stamped the record form for confirmation. The inability of Jingmao Auction House to provide the materials of the other two bidders does not violate the provisions of Article 54, Paragraph 2 of the Auction Law, which states that "the period for keeping auction materials shall be counted from the date of termination of the entrustment auction contract and shall not be less than five years." The requirement of the Guangdong High Court that the auction house provide documents beyond the statutory retention period and bear the legal consequences of inability to provide them is unfounded in law. The court's treatment of pre-registered property rights as debts is the fault of the court and is unrelated to the Applicants for Review. The auction of Guangfeng Building was conducted under the supervision of the Guangdong High Court, and the auction process was open, fair, and lawful. Before the auction, auction notices were published in newspapers four times. There was no fact of malicious collusion between the auction house and the purchaser that harmed the interests of purchasers and other creditors. There is no evidence that Longzheng Company and the auction house used improper means to exclude other bidders from participating in the auction. The law does not prohibit companies whose shareholders are relatives of auction house shareholders from participating in bidding. The Guangdong High Court's finding, in the absence of evidence, that there was malicious collusion and self-selling and self-buying between the bidder and the auction house is erroneous.

This Court opines: An auction conducted upon entrustment by a People's Court is a judicial compulsory auction. Where the People's Court finds errors in the auction, it has the authority to declare the auction void or to set it aside. In this case, the Guangdong High Court found that the shareholders of the purchaser Longzheng Company and Jingmao Auction House were all relatives, indicating an affiliated relationship between the two companies. The Applicants for Review have not denied this, and this Court confirms it. In the presence of an affiliated relationship between Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser due to the kinship of shareholders, unless it can be proven that other unrelated bidders participated in the auction and conducted sufficient competitive bidding, it may be presumed that there was collusion between Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser. The burden of proof for sufficient competitive bidding shall be borne by Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser with which it has an affiliated relationship. In this auction, only one bid was made, and the transaction was concluded at the reserve price, with no competitive bidding. Moreover, the purchaser Longzheng Company and Jingmao Auction House could not provide information on the other two bidders. Upon review, the materials filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce provided by them in the review did not contain any information on the participation of the other two bidders. The fact that the auction materials had passed the retention period is not a reason for their inability to provide information on the bidders. Accordingly, it cannot be determined that other bidders participated in the auction. Hence, it can be determined that there was collusion between Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser Longzheng Company. Since the auction in this case was concluded directly at the reserve price, which was 70% of the market value determined by the appraisal institution, the reasonableness of the appraised price directly affects whether the auction result is fair and reasonable. Regarding the huge discrepancy between the two appraised prices of Guangfeng Building, the Applicants for Review could not provide a reasonable explanation. This Court concurs with the Guangdong High Court's finding that the second appraisal conclusion was obviously unreasonable. Regardless of whether the excessively low appraisal result was the responsibility of the two Applicants for Review, they should have known that the appraised price and transaction price of the subject matter were too low. In this case, the rights relating to Guangfeng Building included claims for delivery of pre-sold units, return of relocated units, refund of purchase money, project payments, bank loans, etc., totaling over RMB 1.5 billion, with only the purchase money registered by purchasers exceeding RMB 200 million. However, the auction price in this case was only RMB 24.12 million, which was of no benefit at all to the enforcement applicant in this case, which had no priority right of compensation, and was clearly a futile auction. Moreover, after the auction, the Guangdong High Court removed all rights burdens relating to Guangfeng Building and transferred the entire building to the purchaser, resulting in the inability to lawfully and effectively protect the rights relating to Guangfeng Building, thereby infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of persons entitled to rights in Guangfeng Building. Since Jingmao Auction House was responsible for receiving declarations of rights relating to Guangfeng Building and the purchaser had an affiliated relationship with it, it can be determined that Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser should also have known of the above issues. Therefore, as to the auction in this case causing infringement upon the rights of persons entitled to rights in Guangfeng Building, Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser Longzheng Company acted with malice.

In summary, the Guangdong High Court correctly determined that the auctioneer Jingmao Auction House and the purchaser Longzheng Company had engaged in malicious collusion in the auction of Guangfeng Building, resulting in the inability to conduct a fair competitive bidding for the auction of Guangfeng Building, thereby harming the interests of purchasers and other creditors. The Enforcement Rulings (1997) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 7-1 and (2011) Yue Gao Fa Zhi Yi Zi No. 1 were not erroneous. The grounds for review of the Applicants for Review cannot be sustained. Pursuant to Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Articles 8 and 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC in Enforcement Proceedings, and upon deliberation by the Judicial Committee of this Court, it is ordered as follows:

The review requests of the Applicants for Review, Guangdong Longzheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. and Guangdong Jingmao Auction House Co., Ltd., are rejected.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Huang Jinlong

Judge: Yu Hong

Acting Judge: Fan Xiangyang

June 15, 2012

Clerk: Huang Lijuan

[Presiding Judge Introduction]

Huang Jinlong, Senior Judge: born in 1964, Master of Laws. Served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2000.
